source.rule: AI 痕迹轻量索引 - 高频优先项

tests.label: signpost fails
tests.input: 更关键的是，成本在上升。

tests.label: direct statement passes
tests.input: 成本在上升。

notes: Chat-domain terms (首先我们需要/值得注意的是/综上所述) already covered by ZS-CHAT-002; excluded here to avoid double-firing.

title: CJK lecture gestures (讲义动作)
summary: De-ai-writing's 伪口语化 lecture gestures: '拆一拆', '盘一盘', '捋一捋', '聊一聊', '划重点', '敲黑板', '说白了', '本质上', '简单来说' — the 'analyst walks you through' voice that LLMs default to when faking approachable tone.

matcher.pattern: 拆一拆|盘一盘|捋一捋|聊一聊|划重点|敲黑板|说白了|本质上|归根结底|简单来说|换个角度看|不妨这样理解|拆开来看|掰开来看|盘点一下|一句话概括|摊开来看|摊开来说

tests.label: lecture gesture fails
tests.input: 我们不妨拆一拆这个问题。

tests.label: direct statement passes
tests.input: 这个问题值得单独讨论。

title: CJK high-frequency analysis verbs (拆解/梳理/剖析...)
summary: De-ai-writing's 高频分析词: '拆解', '梳理', '剖析', '解构', '聚焦', '洞察', '赋能', '驱动' — near-signature verbs of AI Chinese analytical prose; do not stack.

matcher.pattern: 拆解|梳理|剖析|解构|聚焦|洞察|深耕|赋能|助力|践行|驱动|构建|打造

tests.label: stacked verbs fail
tests.input: 本文拆解了三个案例，梳理了关键路径，并剖析了深层原因。

tests.label: plain verbs pass
tests.input: 本文分析了三个案例，给出了具体数据。

notes: Density cap: at most one analysis verb per 40 words, approximating the source's '不要堆叠' rule.

title: CJK correlative stacking (一旦…就 / 只有…才 / 无论…都 / 随着…的 / 通过…来)
summary: De-ai-writing's 关联句式堆叠: over-marked conditionals, universals, and causation — '一旦……就……', '只有……才……', '无论……都……', '随着……的发展', '通过……来……'. Source threshold: max 2 total per piece.

source.rule: AI 高频关联句式堆叠 (7.3)

tests.label: stacked correlatives fail
tests.input: 一旦数据打通，效率就会提升；只有坚持，才能见效；无论多难，都要继续。

tests.label: plain connective passes
tests.input: 数据打通后效率提升，坚持就能见效。

title: CJK dramatized reveal rhetoric (遮羞布/撕下面具/揭开真面目)
summary: De-ai-writing's 戏剧化揭露: '遮羞布', '画皮', '幌子', '烟幕弹', '揭开真面目', '戳穿真相', '撕下面具' — violent-action-plus-concealment metaphors that announce a revelation instead of presenting evidence.

matcher.pattern: 遮羞布|最后一块遮羞布|画皮|幌子|烟幕弹|皇帝的新衣|揭开真面目|戳穿真相|戳穿谎言|撕下面具|剥开外衣|扯下遮羞布|撕开伪装

tests.label: concealment metaphor fails
tests.input: 这不过是给利益输送披了一层遮羞布。

tests.label: mechanism statement passes
tests.input: 利益输送的链条很清楚：A 给 B 拨款，B 给 A 的亲属发合同。

title: CJK extremum judgments (最X的地方在于 / 真正X的是 / …之处在于 / 更X的是)
summary: De-ai-writing's 极值判断: '最残酷的地方在于', '真正可怕的是', '讽刺之处在于', '更可怕的是' — extremum markers that announce the author's insight instead of letting facts land. Source threshold: max 1 per piece.

matcher.pattern: 最[^。！？]{1,16}(地方在于|地方是|的是)|真正(可怕|残酷|讽刺|危险|荒谬|令人不安)的是|(残酷|讽刺|荒谬|吊诡|可怕|麻烦|棘手)之处在于|更(残酷|可怕|讽刺|荒谬|恐怖)的是

source.rule: AI 高频极值判断句式 (7.5)

tests.label: two extremums fail
tests.input: 最残酷的地方在于，淘汰从不提前通知；更讽刺的是，这恰恰是默认流程。

tests.label: single extremum passes
tests.input: 最麻烦的是，数据还没迁移完。

title: CJK pseudo-academic jargon (舆论场/宏大叙事/底层逻辑/抓手/闭环)
summary: De-ai-writing's 伪学术腔: '舆论场', '宏大叙事', '底层逻辑', '认知升级', '降维打击', '抓手', '闭环', '话语权' — social-science and consulting terms used as universal labels, producing fake depth. Source threshold: max 1 total per piece.

matcher.pattern: 舆论场|宏大叙事|底层逻辑|认知升级|降维打击|抓手|闭环|话语权|权柄|顶层设计|路径依赖

tests.label: two terms fail
tests.input: 这背后是舆论场与宏大叙事的博弈。

tests.label: plain claim passes
tests.input: 几家媒体在争论这件事。

notes: Warning tier: 闭环/抓手/路径依赖 are legitimate in engineering and economics registers; the tell is stacking.

title: CJK inanimate-subject negation ('血管不认这些词')
summary: De-ai-writing's 无生命对象拟人化否定: '血管不认这些词', '数据不在乎你的立场', '市场不挑立场' — a short anthropomorphic negation used as a cold aphorism where a mechanism explanation belongs.

matcher.pattern: (血管|数据|历史|算法|市场|分子|病毒|现实|世界|舆论|规则|机制|代码|时间|系统)(不|不会|不肯|不愿|不在乎|不在意|不接受|不认|不挑|不分|不讲|不管|不理)

source.rule: 无生命对象拟人化否定壳 (9.9)

tests.label: vessel negation fails
tests.input: 血管不认这些词。

tests.label: mechanism passes
tests.input: 马兜铃酸进入血液后直接结合肾小管上皮细胞的 DNA。

notes: Warning tier: literal physical statements ('血管不接受过粗的针头') and quoted idioms ('时间不等人') are exempt per the source.

title: CJK web-fiction template words (眼中闪过/嘴角勾起/心头一震...)
summary: Story-deslop's 一级禁用词 for web fiction: '眼中闪过', '嘴角勾起', '眉头微皱', '心中一动', '心头一震', '不容置疑', '不由自主' — template facial/mental beats that replace shown behavior with stock phrases.

matcher.pattern: 眼中闪过|嘴角勾起|眉头微皱|瞳孔微缩|瞳孔收缩|指节泛白|心中一动|心头一震|心中暗道|心底泛起|神色一凛|不由得|不禁|深吸一口气|不容置疑|不容置喙|显而易见|毫无疑问|不由自主|情不自禁|话锋一转

tests.label: template beat fails
tests.input: 他眼中闪过一丝悲伤。

tests.label: shown behavior passes
tests.input: 他垂下眼，把药片放回口袋。

notes: Genre-scoped: web-fiction narrative prose. Replace with concrete action/detail, not another adjective (the source's replacement rule).

title: CJK chapter-end summary beats (这一夜注定/这一切都结束了/新的篇章开始)
summary: Story-deslop's 章末总结体 and trailer-summary patterns: '这一夜注定无人入眠', '这一切都结束了', '新的人生才刚刚开始', '命运的齿轮' — the outline's closing state written out as a summarizing sentence instead of a final action or line.

tests.label: doomed night fails
tests.input: 这一夜，注定无人入眠。

tests.label: action ending passes
tests.input: 她关上了那扇门。没回头。

notes: The source scans only the final ~600 characters; this rule flags any occurrence (safe direction). 这一刻…终于明白 is a normal human cognitive beat in short fiction per the source's calibration — warning tier.

title: CJK trailer endings (没人知道/才刚刚开始/即将来临)
summary: Story-deslop's trailer-ending patterns: '没人知道，这才刚刚开头', '正朝着…压了过来', '拉开序幕', '即将来临' — the narrator previewing the next chapter instead of letting the scene end on a concrete beat.

matcher.pattern: 没人知道|谁也不知道|谁也没想到|殊不知|(这)?才刚刚开(始|头)|(?<!正式)拉开(序幕|帷幕)|即将(开始|来临|降临)|正(朝着|向着)[^。！？!?\n]{0,24}(压|涌|袭|逼)(了?过去|了?过来|来)

tests.label: nobody knows fails
tests.input: 没人知道，这才刚刚开头。

tests.label: concrete beat passes
tests.input: 他在门口站了一会儿，推门走了。

notes: Lookbehind (?<!正式) spares the standard phrase '正式拉开序幕'. The source restricts to the final 600 characters; this flags any occurrence (safe direction).

title: CJK voice-contrast template (声音不大…却…)
summary: Story-deslop's 音量反差腔: '声音不大，却带着…', '声音不高，第一句却…' — the AI-favorite voice description that pads volume then pivots; delete the volume setup and write the actual sound or effect.

tests.label: voice contrast fails
tests.input: 她的声音不大，却带着不容置疑的力量。

tests.label: direct voice passes
tests.input: 她压低声音说完了那句话。

title: Mic-drop pause commands ('Read that again.', 'Let that sink in.')
summary: A one-sentence paragraph that tells the reader to pause on a claim instead of adding to it ('That is the real win.', 'Read that again.', 'Let that sink in.') is the humanizer skill's second-strongest tell; the same closer reappearing after several sections is worse. Delete the line or merge it into a sentence that carries a new fact.

source.rule: **Watch for:** a one-sentence paragraph that restates the paragraph before it; "That is the real win."; "That distinction matters."; "Read that again."; "Let that sink in."; the same closer after several sections; ... **Problem:** The line asks the reader to pause on a claim instead of adding to it.

tests.label: fails - pause-command closer
tests.input:
Caching cuts repeat work.

That is the real win.

Read that again.

tests.label: passes - closers carry facts
tests.input: Caching cuts repeat work. Retries hide brief outages.

notes: 'That distinction matters.' is already covered by ZS-PROSE-030; do not reopen the question of one-off emphasis sentences that carry a new fact.

title: Post-example moralizing ('This shows the importance of...')
summary: A sentence placed after an example, scene, or number that names what it showed restates the reader's own inference; the 3.1.0 humanizer release extended this pattern explicitly. Keep the example, cut the lesson, unless the sentence adds a consequence the example did not.

source.rule: a sentence after an example, scene, or number that names what it showed ("This shows the importance of...", "The message was clear:", "It was a lesson in patience.") ... Cut a closer that repeats, including one that explains an example the reader just saw.
Extended #2 to "That distinction matters." (#277) and to a sentence that explains what an example already showed (#295).

tests.label: fails - moralizing after the example
tests.input: The rollout took three weeks and broke twice in production. This shows the importance of staging.

tests.label: passes - example carries its own consequence
tests.input: The rollout took three weeks and broke twice, both times in the staging environment we had skipped.

title: Aphorism formulas ('X is the language of Y', 'X becomes a trap')
summary: An ordinary point dressed as a hidden truth: the copula-plus-metaphor 'X is the language/currency/architecture of Y' and 'X becomes a trap' add weight without adding a claim. Replace the saying with the specific claim it gestures at.

source.rule: **Watch for:** the real question is, at its core, in reality, what really matters, fundamentally, the deeper issue, the heart of the matter, X is the Y of Z, X becomes a trap, X is not a tool but a mirror, the language of, the currency of, the architecture of. **Problem:** An ordinary point is dressed as a hidden truth or an aphorism, and the dressing adds no detail.

tests.label: fails - aphorism formulas
tests.input: Symmetry is the language of trust. Efficiency becomes a trap when teams forget the human layer.

tests.label: passes - specific claim
tests.input: Symmetric layouts often feel more predictable to users. Teams can over-optimize workflows and miss how people actually use them.

notes: The copula is required, so plain technical uses ('the architecture of the service is layered') do not match. 'the real question is' is already covered by ZS-PROSE-077.

title: Arguing with an objection nobody made
summary: The text rejects an option or answers an objection that appears nowhere in it — 'This isn't about X', 'I'm not saying Y', 'A tempting approach would be Z' — usually a leftover from an earlier draft. Remove the defense; if it holds a real claim, state the claim.

terms: it would be easy to just

source.rule: **Watch for:** This isn't (mainly) about, I'm not saying, To be clear, Don't get me wrong, This is not to say, Some might say... but, A tempting approach would be, One might be tempted to, An obvious approach would be, You might think... but, It would be easy to just. **Problem:** The text answers an objection or rejects an option that appears nowhere else, usually a leftover from an earlier draft.

tests.label: fails - self-defense and fake alternative
tests.input: This isn't about prompt length, and I'm not saying documentation does not matter. A tempting approach would be to rotate tokens on a cron job.

tests.label: passes - states the claim
tests.input: The issue is whether the agent can use the instruction when it acts. Tokens rotate in place and clients refresh transparently.

notes: 'To be clear' is in the upstream watch list but is left out here: it fires on legitimate clarifications often enough to be noise. Keep it for review, not for this rule.

title: Hyphenated compound modifiers after the noun
summary: Compound modifiers keep their hyphen in every position; the hyphen belongs only before the noun. 'the report is high-quality' should be 'the report is high quality'. Weak alone, so info tier — but the source's six watched words are wrong every time they follow a copula.

source.rule: **Watch for:** high-quality, well-known, well-documented, long-term, real-time, client-facing after the noun they describe. **Problem:** Compound modifiers keep their hyphen in every position. Keep the hyphen before a noun, as in `a high-quality report`, and drop it after the noun, as in `the report is high quality`.

tests.label: fails - hyphen after the noun
tests.input: The report is high-quality, the process is well-documented, and the plan is long-term.

tests.label: passes - hyphen only before the noun
tests.input: The report is high quality, the process is well documented, and the plan is long term.

notes: Only the six words the source watches are matched, so dictionary-hyphenated terms such as third-party and cross-functional stay untouched.

title: Vague capability phrasing ('helps with', 'can be used for')
summary: Describing what a thing does as 'helps with X' or 'can be used for Y' states a capability without stating it. Both the tool-design and skill-authoring guidance in the context-engineering corpus ban these as the canonical vague description.

source.rule: What does the tool do? State exactly what the tool accomplishes -- avoid vague language like "helps with" or "can be used for."
Avoid vague descriptions like these: description: Helps with documents / description: Processes data

tests.label: fails - capability never stated
tests.input: The summarize tool helps with documents and can be used for reporting tasks.

tests.label: passes - states the behavior
tests.input: The summarize tool returns a 120-word summary of a document's main claims.

notes: Bare 'help with' is deliberately absent: it fires on ordinary instructions ('ask someone to help with the migration'). 'is useful for' is the same unnamed-capability move.

title: Plans and docs: no lines that decide nothing
summary: Instruction lines that commit to no decision — 'handle edge cases', 'add appropriate validation', 'write tests for the above'. Superpowers' writing-plans calls these 'the opposite failure' of an over-written plan: a plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone, so a line with no decision in it is a gap, not a plan step.

source.rule: Lines that decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation", "write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the opposite failure
Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing ... a line that decides nothing is a gap

tests.label: decision-free step fails
tests.input:
## Task 3
- Wire the new endpoint into the router.
- Add appropriate validation and handle edge cases.

tests.label: concrete step passes
tests.input:
## Task 3
- Route `POST /v1/retry` to `retryHandler` in `src/router.ts`, ahead of the catch-all.
- Reject payloads over 1 MiB with 413 in `parseBody`; test with a 2 MiB body.

tests.label: spec that names its cases passes
tests.input: Where the flow is not ordered, `mergeRules` keeps the caller's order; the provider list is consulted only when `--registry` is passed.

notes: Scope is plan/spec/instruction prose. Deliberate hedges in requirements ('where jurisdiction requires') are a purpose-gate call; the tell is a step that hands the decision back without naming the case. 'TBD' filler is already ZS-INTEGRITY-008, so this rule targets the verb-led phrasings instead.

title: No redundant trailing source or reference list
summary: An answer or doc that already cites inline and then appends a block of 'Sources:', 'References:', 'Further reading:', or 'Citations:' duplicates the same links in a second form. The last30days output contract omits these lists anywhere in the response and keeps only the inline links; the block is a filler artifact, not evidence.

source.rule: Omit duplicate `Sources:`, `References:`, `Further reading:`, and `Citations:` lists anywhere in the response; honor an explicit user request for one.
A saved appendix or source-count footer never replaces required visible citations.

tests.label: trailing source list fails
tests.input:
Docker's Compose watch mode shipped in the 2.22 release.

**Further reading:**

- [Compose watch docs](https://docs.docker.com/compose/file-watch/)
- [Release notes](https://docs.docker.com/compose/release-notes/)

tests.label: inline-only citations pass
tests.input: Docker's Compose watch mode shipped in the [2.22 release](https://docs.docker.com/compose/release-notes/) and syncs on file change.

tests.label: prose mentioning sources passes
tests.input: The sources disagree: two threads say the rollback shipped, one says it was reverted the same week.

notes: Upstream allows the list when the user asks for one; the trigger is a heading or label line that only re-lists links already inline. A one-line inline 'Source: …' attributing a single figure is not this tell.

title: Therapeutic or validating language ('I hear you', 'give yourself grace')
summary: Emotional-support filler in written output — 'I hear you', 'That sounds hard', 'You're valid', 'Give yourself grace', 'Be kind to yourself'. The beautiful-prose skill lists therapeutic or validating language under absolute prohibitions, and its quality bar cuts every sentence that exists to guide the reader's emotions: the tell is a sentence that soothes instead of informing.

source.rule: 4) Therapeutic or validating language — No: "I hear you" / "That sounds hard" / "You're valid" / "Give yourself grace" / "Be kind to yourself"
Remove any sentence that exists to guide the reader's emotions.

tests.label: validation filler fails
tests.input: I hear you - that deadline was brutal. Give yourself grace this week and be kind to yourself.

tests.label: plain report passes
tests.input: The deadline slipped by four days; the release moved with it and nothing else changed.

notes: The ban is on a sentence whose function is emotional management, not on empathy itself: a direct acknowledgement that names the fact ('the vendor missed the SLA twice') is unaffected. Transcripts of a human conversation, quoted support replies, and user-requested warmth are exclusion zones.

title: Skill descriptions: no first-person or 'This skill does' framing
summary: A SKILL.md frontmatter description written as self-description — 'description: I can help you with async tests when they're flaky' or 'This skill does X and Y' — breaks the third-person, trigger-first contract: the description is injected into a system prompt and exists so the agent can decide whether to load the skill, not to narrate what the skill contains.

source.rule: ❌ BAD: First person — description: I can help you with async tests when they're flaky
Use imperative phrasing. Frame it as an instruction to the agent: "Use this skill when..." rather than "This skill does..."
Write in third person (injected into system prompt)

tests.label: first-person description fails
tests.input:
---
name: async-test-helpers
description: I can help you with async tests when they're flaky
---

# Async test helpers

tests.label: trigger-first description passes
tests.input:
---
name: async-test-helpers
description: Use when tests have race conditions, timing dependencies, or pass and fail inconsistently
---

# Async test helpers

tests.label: prose first person passes
tests.input: I can help you with the migration if you want, but the schema change is the real blocker.

notes: Anchored to a `description:` line so ordinary prose that opens a sentence with 'I can' is untouched. The complementary half of the contract — never summarising the workflow in the description — is a skillNote, not a matcher.

title: Filler phrases: vague timeframes, soft quantifiers, and idle attention claims
summary: anti-slop-writing's filler list names phrases that add length without information: 'in recent years' (give the actual years), 'a wide range of' (name what is in the range), 'dive deep into' (just discuss it), 'take a closer look at', 'needless to say', 'more often than not', 'last but not least', plus the vague-attention phrases 'inherent tensions' and 'this raises important questions about'.

source.rule: **Common AI filler phrases (cut or replace):** … "a wide range of" → name what's in the range | "needless to say" → cut | "more often than not" → "usually" or give a number | "take a closer look at" → cut or be direct | "at this point in time" → "now" | "in recent years" → give the actual years or timeframe | "dive deep into" → just discuss it

unsupported intensifiers → add evidence or delete | "one thing is clear" | "the key takeaway" | "inherent tensions" | "this raises important questions about" | stacked hedging adverbs → state the supported level of certainty

tests.label: filler stack fails
tests.input: In recent years a wide range of teams have taken a closer look at the scheduler, and more often than not they dive deep into the config file.

tests.label: concrete sentence passes
tests.input: Since 2023, four teams have reviewed the scheduler. Two of them changed the config file and cut p99 latency to 40ms.

notes: Upstream frames its lists as review prompts, not hard bans (keep the phrase when it is the accurate wording), so this is warning tier. 'at this point in time' and 'it goes without saying' are already ZS-PROSE-045/013.

title: English fiction template n-grams (slop-list bigrams and trigrams)
summary: slop-score ships the word and n-gram lists it matches LLM writing against for overuse relative to a human baseline. Its bigram/trigram lists are body-language and scene-template phrases ('casting long shadows', 'heart pounding', 'eyes narrowed', 'dimly lit'); our DB covers the CJK equivalents (ZS-PROSE-116) but has nothing for English fiction.

source.rule: casting long shadows | long shadows across | heart pounding | pounding chest | dimly lit | room fell silent
heart pounding | mind racing | eyes widened | eyes narrowed | brow furrowed | voice trembling | barely audible
Slop List Matches — its writing is matched to a precomputed list of words and trigrams which are overused in AI text compared to human baselines.

tests.label: template body language fails
tests.input: She stepped into the dimly lit corridor, heart pounding, casting long shadows behind her as the door shut.

tests.label: plain action passes
tests.input: She walked into the corridor and checked the gauge on the wall. Then she shut the door.

notes: Terms are taken verbatim from the upstream lists; entries that are only artifacts of upstream preprocessing (e.g. 'shook head' from 'shook his head') were dropped so the phrases match real prose. Warning tier because this is a detector list, not a hard ban.

title: Indonesian formulaic AI shells (temporal frame, epistemic padding, not-only contrast)
summary: anti-slop-writing's Indonesian reference names language-specific shells that mirror English AI tells: the 'Di era modern ini' temporal frame, the 'dapat dilihat bahwa / dipahami bahwa' padding, the compulsory 'dengan demikian, dapat disimpulkan' ending, 'merupakan salah satu X yang paling Y' importance inflation, the 'tidak hanya … tetapi juga' contrast, and the 'Di sisi lain, terdapat … tantangan' pivot. Our DB has CJK and English detection families but no Indonesian entry.

matcher.pattern: di era modern ini|seiring perkembangan zaman|dalam konteks globalisasi|dapat dilihat bahwa|dapat dipahami bahwa|perlu dipahami bahwa|dapat disimpulkan|merupakan salah satu[^.]{0,40}yang paling|tidak hanya[^.]{0,60}tetapi juga|di sisi lain[,，]\s*terdapat

source.rule: Temporal framing such as "Di era modern ini" can delay the point when the specific context is not needed. … Seiring perkembangan zaman, semakin banyak orang yang menyadari pentingnya... | Dalam konteks globalisasi yang terus berkembang...

Passive epistemic constructions such as "dapat dilihat bahwa" can add words without adding information. … Dari data tersebut, dapat dilihat bahwa terdapat peningkatan yang signifikan. | Dapat dipahami bahwa fenomena ini merupakan cerminan… | Perlu dipahami bahwa konteks ini sangat penting…

Dengan demikian, dapat disimpulkan bahwa festival ini memiliki peran penting dalam melestarikan budaya lokal … | Jakarta merupakan salah satu kota dengan perkembangan ekonomi yang paling pesat di Asia Tenggara. | Pelatihan ini tidak hanya meningkatkan kompetensi peserta, tetapi juga memperkuat jaringan profesional mereka. | Di sisi lain, terdapat beberapa tantangan yang perlu diatasi

tests.label: temporal frame fails
tests.input: Di era modern ini, teknologi memainkan peran yang semakin krusial dalam kehidupan manusia.

tests.label: not-only contrast fails
tests.input: Pelatihan ini tidak hanya meningkatkan kompetensi peserta, tetapi juga memperkuat jaringan profesional mereka.

tests.label: direct statement passes
tests.input: Pelatihan ini meningkatkan kompetensi peserta dan memperkuat jaringan profesional mereka. Sepuluh peserta pindah ke peran teknis sejak Juli.

notes: Upstream marks every BI check as an editorial prompt, not an authorship indicator, so warning tier. 'di mana' as a relative pronoun (BI-8) was left out: legitimate as an interrogative and too false-positive-prone for a scan.

title: Corporate catchphrases (office jargon starters)
summary: Business catchphrases that only ever appear in copy written to sound corporate: 'hit the ground running', 'low-hanging fruit', 'take this offline'. proselint ships this exact list as industrial_language.corporate_speak.

source.rule: message="Minimize your use of corporate catchphrases like '{}'." items=("hit the ground running", "get the ball rolling", "low-hanging fruit", "thrown under the bus", "think outside the box", "it's on my radar", "no brainer", "par for the course", "bang for your buck", "move the goal post", "apples to apples", "win-win", "all hands on deck", "take this offline", "drill-down", "elephant in the room", "on my plate")

tests.label: fails
tests.input: Let's get the ball rolling on the pricing page, then empty the low-hanging fruit backlog.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: We can start on the pricing page this week, then clear the small backlog items.

notes: Excludes terms already covered elsewhere in the DB (at the end of the day -> ZS-PROSE-008, synergy / touch base -> ZS-PROSE-013). Business register is sometimes deliberate, hence warning.

title: Commercialese and bureaucratese letter-speak
summary: Pre-email office register ('please be advised that', 'enclosed herewith', 'regret to inform') that resurfaces when a model imitates formal correspondence. proselint files these as commercialese/jargon; LanguageTool keeps the same phrases as plain-English style rules.

terms: your favor has come to hand

source.rule: message="'{}' is commercialese." items=("acknowledging yours of", "beg to advise", "enclosed herewith", "enclosed please find", "pending receipt of", "please be advised that", "please return same", "pursuant to your request", "regret to inform", "thanking you in advance", "the undersigned", "we are pleased to note")
message="'{}' is jargon. Can you replace it with something more standard?" items=("in the affirmative", "in the negative", "agendize", "per your order", "per your request", "disincentivize")

AS_PER: Business jargon meaning 'in accordance with'. Replace with 'as' … AT_YOUR_EARLIEST_CONVENIENCE: Overly formal. Did you mean 'as soon as you can'? … UNTIL_SUCH_TIME_AS: Use 'until'. … YOU_ARE_REQUESTED: Replace with 'please'

tests.label: fails
tests.input: Please be advised that the invoice enclosed herewith is pending receipt of your approval.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: The invoice attached to this email is waiting for your approval.

notes: 'with regard to' is already ZS-PROSE-045 and is omitted here; 'as per' overlaps ZS-PROSE-014's term 'as per my last email' but is a distinct tell (business-letter register).

title: Chat-speak abbreviations and slackened spellings
summary: Messaging abbreviations and informal spellings leaking into published prose ('btw', 'ttyl', 'wanna', 'gimme'). proselint ships the abbreviation list as chatspeak; LanguageTool flags the same class as informal register.

source.rule: message="'{}' is chatspeak. Write it out." items=("2day", "4U", "AFAIK", "ASAP", "B4", "brb", "btw", "GR8", "lol", "OMG", "sum1", "THX", "TTYL", "XOXO")

OUTTA: The word '\1' is informal. … LEMME: The word '\1' is informal. … GIMME: The word "\1" is informal. … WANNA_TO: The word 'wanna' is informal, consider replacing it. … ANYWAYS: The word '\1' is informal American English. … PPL: The abbreviation for 'people' can be considered informal.

tests.label: fails
tests.input: btw the deploy finished, wanna take a look? ttyl

tests.label: passes
tests.input: The deploy finished; let me know if you want to review the logs.

notes: Excludes LanguageTool's DAT/DIS entries, which flag dialect forms rather than slop.

title: RAS syndrome (redundant acronym expansions)
summary: 'PIN number', 'ATM machine', 'PDF format' — an acronym followed by the word it already contains. proselint ships this list verbatim; vale keeps the same tokens in its built-in Redundancy style.

source.rule: message="RAS syndrome. Use '{}' instead of '{}'." items=("abm missile", "abs braking system", "atm machine", "cd disc", "cpi Index", "gps system", "gui interface", "hiv virus", "isbn number", "lcd display", "pdf format", "pin number", "please RSVP", "rip in peace", "sat test", "upc codes")
message: "'%s' is redundant" … - ATM machine / - CD disc / - GPS system / - GUI interface / - PDF format / - PIN number

tests.label: fails
tests.input: Enter your PIN number, then the ATM machine prints the PDF format summary.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: Enter your PIN, then the ATM prints the PDF summary.

title: Pleonasms (redundant modifier-noun pairs)
summary: Pairs where one word restates the other: 'end result', 'added bonus', 'past history', 'true fact'. LanguageTool ships them as a bad=good redundancy database and vale keeps the same tokens as an error-level style rule.

source.rule: 12 noon=noon / absolute guarantee=guarantee / actual fact=fact / added bonus=bonus / advance notice=notice / advance planning=planning / armed gunman=gunman / end result=result / filled to capacity=filled / natural instinct=instinct / new invention=invention / personal opinion=opinion / plan ahead=plan / repeat again=repeat / revert back=revert / safe haven=haven / sum total=total / total destruction=destruction / true fact=fact / unexpected surprise=surprise / usual custom=custom

message: "'%s' is redundant" tokens: - (?:added|extra) bonus / - (?:terrible|horrible) tragedy / - absolutely (?:necessary|essential) / - brief (?:moment|summary) / - combine … together / - end result / - false pretense / - final result / - free gift / - join together / - natural instinct / - new invention / - past history / - safe haven / - shout loudly / - unexpected surprise / - unintended mistake / - violent explosion

tests.label: fails
tests.input: The end result was an added bonus, and a true fact is that we should plan ahead to avoid an unexpected surprise.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: The result helped, and we should plan the next release so surprises stay rare.

notes: 'close proximity' and 'still remains' are omitted — already covered by ZS-PROSE-090 / ZS-PROSE-094.

title: Uncomparable adjectives with intensifiers ('very unique')
summary: Intensifiers glued onto adjectives that already carry the maximum ('very unique', 'most perfect', 'increasingly inevitable'). proselint generates the pair set programmatically; LanguageTool has a dedicated VERY_UNIQUE rule.

source.rule: CHECK_MESSAGE = "Comparison of an uncomparable: '{}' is not comparable." / COMPARATORS = ("extremely", "increasingly", "kind of", "largely", "less", "mildly", "more", "quite", "very") / UNCOMPARABLES = ("absolute", "complete", "fatal", "ideal", "impossible", "inevitable", "perfect", "unique", …)
quite unique=unique / almost unique=not unique / very necessary=necessary / very relevant=relevant / very true=true

tests.label: fails
tests.input: This is a very unique setup, and the failure was increasingly inevitable.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: This setup differs from everything else we run, and the failure looked likely.

notes: 'complete'/'entire' are deliberately absent: 'more complete' is ordinary English. 'paramount' overlaps ZS-PROSE-002 but only in the intensifier-pair form here.

title: Litotes (negative understatement)
summary: Understatement built by negating the opposite: 'not bad', 'not unlike', 'not certain'. vale ships these as substitution swaps (not bad -> good) and LanguageTool keeps the same class as NOT_* rules that tell you to drop the 'not'.

source.rule: extends: substitution … swap: no ordinary: extraordinary / not (?:a)? bad: good / not certain: uncertain / not many: few / not the same: different / not unaware: aware / not unlike: like / not unpleasant: pleasant / not useless: useful / not wrong: right

NOT_CERTAIN: Avoid using "not". Did you mean 'uncertain'? … NOT_UNLIKE: Avoid using "not". Did you mean 'similar' or 'alike'? … NOT_MANY: Avoid using "not". Did you mean 'few'? … NOT_THE_SAME: Avoid using "not". Did you mean 'different'? … NOT_ABLE: Avoid using "not". Did you mean 'unable'? … NOT_VERY_OFTEN: Avoid using "not". Did you mean 'seldom', 'rare' or 'not often'?

tests.label: fails
tests.input: The result was not bad, and the migration path was not unlike what we shipped last year.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: The result was good, and the migration path matched last year's rollout.

notes: 'not without' is omitted: ZS-PROSE-094 already owns the 'it's not without its challenges' construction.

title: Paragraphs that open with 'But'
summary: proselint encodes the editing rule 'No paragraph should start with a But.' — a transition convention that AI drafts break constantly.

tests.label: fails
tests.input:
The first pass came back clean.

But the second pass failed on line 40.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: The first pass came back clean, but the second pass failed on line 40.

notes: Case-sensitive on purpose: proselint's engine runs this check with case_insensitive=False, so only the capitalised opener is flagged.

title: 'In recent years, an increasing number of X have' opener
summary: Templated scholarly opener that announces a trend instead of a finding. proselint files it as misc.narcissism: 'Talk about the subject, not its study.'

matcher.pattern: \bin recent years, an increasing number of\b|\ban increasing number of [A-Za-z]{3,}sts have\b

source.rule: check_type=types.ExistenceSimple(pattern="In recent years, an increasing number of [a-zA-Z]{3,}sts have") … message="Professional narcissism. Talk about the subject, not its study."

tests.label: fails
tests.input: In recent years, an increasing number of researchers have revisited the pricing question.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: Since 2019 the pricing question has drawn more attention from researchers.

title: Hyperbolic punctuation stacks (!!, ??)
summary: Doubled or tripled sentence punctuation. proselint flags it as hyperbole; vale ships the same two patterns in its ported proselint style.

tests.label: fails
tests.input: This release is huge!!

tests.label: passes
tests.input: This release is significant.

notes: Complements ZS-PROSE-020 (single '!' budget per 1,000 words) — this one catches the stacked form.

title: Job-posting jargon (ninja, rock star, meritocracy)
summary: Recruiter slang that devalues the role and signals a company-written ad: 'rock star', 'ninja', 'guru', 'meritocracy', 'drama-free'. vale ships these as the Joblint style; it is the only prose surface code agents usually write besides docs.

source.rule: message: "Avoid using '%s'" description: "Referring to tech people as '%s' devalues the work that they do…" tokens: 'gurus?' / 'hero(?:es|ic)?' / 'ninjas?' / 'rock[ -]*stars?' / 'super[ -]*stars?' / 'badass(?:es)?' / 'BAMF'

message: "Avoid using '%s'" description: "Something feels off when you need to reassure someone of something that should definitely not be an issue in any workplace." tokens: 'drama[ -]*free' / 'stress[ -]*free'

tests.label: fails
tests.input: We need a rock star ninja for a drama-free team.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: We are hiring a backend engineer to own the scheduler and the review rotation.

notes: Joblint's Gendered / Derogatory / Hair / Sexualised lists are bias checks, not slop tells, and are left out. Terms with legitimate technical or general-prose readings (greenfield, blue sky, hardcore, heroic, enlightened, juggle, tight deadlines, hella) are dropped from vale's tokens to keep the rule from firing on ordinary engineering prose and dialect.

title: Archaic and mock-archaic diction
summary: 'Methinks', 'forsooth', 'peradventure', 'to wit' — costume-drama diction that shows up in generated historical prose and in legalese residue. proselint flags the list as archaism; LanguageTool flags the adverbial cousin ('fastly') as archaic.

source.rule: message="'{}' is archaic." items=("alack", "anent", "begat", "belike", "betimes", "cozen", "fain", "forsooth", "haply", "howbeit", "illumine", "in sooth", "methinks", "peradventure", "perchance", "saith", "shew", "spake", "to wit", "verily", "whilom", "withal")
<rule id="FASTLY" name="fastly (quickly)"> … The adverb "fastly" is considered archaic. Consider an alternative.
message="The 'from' in 'from whence' is not needed."

tests.label: fails
tests.input: Methinks the plan will hold, forsooth.

tests.label: passes
tests.input: I think the plan will hold.

notes: 'divers' / 'nigh' / 'wot' are omitted from proselint's list — too many legitimate readings in modern prose.

title: LinkedIn ritual vocabulary (personal news, a new chapter, bittersweet)
summary: Career-post ritual phrases announce the announcement instead of the fact. They cluster so tightly that a post carrying three of them reads as a filled-in template rather than news.

matcher.pattern: \b(?:personal news|a new chapter|the next chapter|bittersweet|with mixed emotions|(?:humbled|thrilled|excited|delighted|honored|honoured) to announce|this is your sign|today years old|i['’]ll go first|(?:couldn['’]?t|could not) be (?:more proud|prouder|happier|more thrilled))

source.rule: LinkedIn ritual: "some personal news", "a new chapter", "bittersweet", "couldn't be prouder", "this is your sign", "I'll go first", "today years old" | The fact, then stop; feeling shown through detail
personal-news: \b(?:some )?personal news[:.]|\b(?:big|exciting) news[:.]|\b(?:a new|the next) chapter\b|\bbittersweet\b|\bwith mixed emotions\b
couldnt-be-prouder: \bcould(?:n(?:'|’)t| not) be (?:more proud|prouder|more excited|happier|more thrilled)\b

tests.label: ritual post fails
tests.input: Some personal news: after nine years on the platform team I'm moving on. A bittersweet week, and I couldn't be prouder of what we shipped.

tests.label: plain notice passes
tests.input: After nine years on the platform team I'm leaving on Friday. The handover doc is in the shared drive, and Priya takes the on-call rotation.

notes: Tier is warning, not error: "a new chapter" is legitimate in book and fiction prose, so this fires on register, not on grammar. Scope to social/career posts and personal announcements.

title: Engagement-bait asks (drop a comment, link in bio, what's your take)
summary: Closing the piece with a request for likes, comments or tags substitutes reach for a conclusion. The ask is the only part of the writing aimed at the algorithm instead of the reader.

terms: let me know in the comments

source.rule: engagement-bait: \b(?:agree\?|thoughts\?|what(?:'|’)s your (?:take|experience)|drop a comment|let me know in the comments|share this with|share if you|tag someone|repost if|follow (?:me|for more)|sound off in|save this post|bookmark this|link in (?:bio|the )?(?:first )?comments?|dm me\b|comment ... and i'll|my dms are (?:always )?open|what about you\?)\b

tests.label: bait closer fails
tests.input: If this landed for you, drop a comment. And what's your take on the pricing change?

tests.label: factual closer passes
tests.input: Pricing changed on Tuesday. The invoice page now shows the new rate before checkout, so nobody signs blind.

notes: "bookmark this", "save this for later" and "don't sleep on this" already live in ZS-PROSE-081; excluded here to avoid double-counting one closer twice.

title: Performed-writer slang (has receipts, vibe check, rent-free)
summary: Slang-cute idiom is a costume: the writer impersonates a punchy human voice instead of stating the evidence. The same family arrives when rewriting machinery strips real slop and adds stagey colloquialism.

matcher.pattern: \b(?:vibe check|just a vibe|on vibes|with vibes|vibes-based|(?:has|have|got) (?:the )?receipts|living rent-free|rent-free in (?:my|your|his|her|their|our) head|on the tin|minding (?:its|their|his|her) own business)\b

source.rule: Slang-cute idiom: "has receipts", "hits different", "living rent-free" | State the evidence itself; see the slang-costume ban in overcorrection.md
Slang costume — forced colloquialisms a professional author wouldn't use ("chef's kiss", "hits different") unless the voice sample has them
has-receipts: \b(?:has|got) receipts\b|\bthe receipts to prove it\b ; vibe-register: \b(?:is|isn(?:'|’)t|was|not|just) a vibe\b|\bvibe check\b|\bwith vibes\b

tests.label: slang costume fails
tests.input: The scorer is a meter you can argue with, and it has receipts.

tests.label: plain statement passes
tests.input: The scorer reports the count and lists every matched phrase.

notes: warning, not error: these are legitimate in a voice that already uses them. "hits different" is deliberately absent — it is already listed in ZS-PROSE-089.

title: Hyperbole universals (nothing on earth, known to man)
summary: Universal hyperbole asserts importance by widening the claim past anything checkable. The honest comparison is always smaller and stronger.

source.rule: Hyperbole universals: "nothing on earth", "on the planet", "in history", "known to man" | State the actual scope; the honest comparison is smaller and stronger

tests.label: universal hyperbole fails
tests.input: Nothing on earth prepares you for a 3am pager when the failover path is untested.

tests.label: scoped claim passes
tests.input: The rollback took eleven minutes, longer than the quarterly drill suggested.

notes: The pattern is deliberately narrow: bare "in history" or "on the planet" alone are not matched, only the nothing/nobody/nowhere + universal-scope collocation.

title: 'X and Y alike' audience formula
summary: The 'beginners and experts alike' formula asserts universal appeal without naming a single user. It is a stock marketing cadence, not a claim.

tests.label: audience formula fails
tests.input: The new editor is a win for beginners and experts alike.

tests.label: named audiences pass
tests.input: Beginners get a wizard; experts get the config file.

notes: warning: the construction is legitimate when the two audiences are genuinely addressed later in the piece; the tell is promising both without evidence.

title: Invented compound labels (the X paradox, the X trap)
summary: AI appends abstract problem-nouns to domain words and then uses them as if they were established, rigorously defined terms. One is a coinage; several in one piece is a strong machine signal.

source.rule: Invented compound labels — AI appends abstract problem-nouns (paradox, trap, creep, divide, vacuum, inversion) to domain words - 'supervision paradox', 'acceleration trap', 'workload creep' - and uses them as if they're established, rigorously defined terms. Multiple such labels in the same piece is a strong signal of AI slop.

Jargon compression: invented compound terms in place of explanation — "threshold cliff", "length-blind floor", "pinned high forever" | Unpack into the plain explanation once, then a short name only if the document truly reuses it; the fix is unpacking, not a synonym

tests.label: two coinages fail
tests.input: The supervision paradox explains the acceleration trap that every platform team eventually hits.

tests.label: one plain mechanism passes
tests.input: Reviewers who own the service approve faster than a central board does. We moved the queue to the owning team.

tests.label: article plus noun is not a label
tests.input: The init script is a trap for anyone who copies it without reading. It was the vacuum the old build left behind.

notes: Capped at one label per 500 words because "poverty trap" and "digital divide" are real established terms; only the density is a signal, matching the upstream wording "Multiple such labels in the same piece". Determiners are excluded before the noun so a plain "a trap" is never counted (second pass fixture is the regression test for that guard).

title: Generic benefit stack (platform/tool + two interchangeable benefits)
summary: A product noun paired with two or more interchangeable outcomes (more value, greater efficiency, strong capabilities) is a stack of benefits with no named capability behind it. Upstream scores this by proximity, not by keywords alone.

source.rule: Generic benefit stack: a platform, product, or service is paired with two or more interchangeable outcomes such as "more value", "greater efficiency", or "strong capabilities" | Replace the stack with one named capability, measured result, or specific use case; ask for the missing fact rather than inventing it

tests.label: benefit stack fails
tests.input: Our platform helps teams ship faster, combining deep experience with the capabilities they need to grow.

tests.label: named capability passes
tests.input: The tool reads a CSV and writes Parquet in about forty seconds on a laptop.

notes: The upstream Python pattern uses inline (?is) flags, which are not valid in JavaScript; the dotAll behaviour is spelled [\s\S] and the 260-character proximity window is preserved unchanged.

title: Temporal hedge ladder (currently, at the time of writing, as of now)
summary: Stacked time-disclaimers cancel each other out: two or three hedges about when the writer is writing replace one statement of when the fact was true.

matcher.pattern: (?:currently|at the time of writing|as of (?:this|the present) (?:writing|moment)|as of now|at present|for now|right now)[^.!?\n]{0,40}?(?:currently|at the time of writing|as of (?:this|the present) (?:writing|moment)|as of now|at present)

source.rule: Temporal hedge ladders — Problem: Stacked time-disclaimers cancel each other out. Before: "Currently, at the time of writing, as of the present moment, the field appears to be evolving rapidly." After: "The field changed substantially between 2020 and 2026."

tests.label: stacked time hedges fail
tests.input: Currently, at the time of writing, the API is unstable under load.

tests.label: dated statement passes
tests.input: The API was unstable in March and settled down after the shard split.

notes: Scans within one sentence only (the [^.!?\n] bridge never crosses a sentence end); a temporal adverb alone is punctuation, not a tell.

title: Manuscript boilerplate (to the best of our knowledge, fills a critical gap)
summary: Academic framing phrases that promise novelty or completeness instead of stating scope. They signal a draft generated to fill space, and a reviewer can always see through them.

terms: to the best of our knowledge
to the best of the authors' knowledge

source.rule: Manuscript boilerplate — Opening phrases that signal a draft AI generated to fill space. Phrases to watch: "To the best of our knowledge", "fills a critical gap in the literature", "represents a significant advance", "of paramount importance", "constitutes the first comprehensive [X]", "lays the foundation for".

tests.label: boilerplate claim fails
tests.input: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to characterise the failure mode.

tests.label: scope stated directly passes
tests.input: No published study has characterised this failure mode. We ran 24 trials across two racks.

notes: "of paramount importance" and "represents a significant advance" were dropped from the list: "paramount" is already banned by ZS-PROSE-005 and the advance/inflection framing by ZS-PROSE-029.

title: Nominalization chains (the implementation of the policy)
summary: Translationese and machine prose turn verbs into abstract nouns and then chain them with 'of'. Density is the signal: each chain replaces a sentence someone could act on.

source.rule: F-4 | Sino-Korean nominalizers -성/-적/-화 plus literal English -tion/-ment/-ness/-ity, 12+ per document | Restore verb and adjective roots: "the implementation of the policy" → 정책 시행
F-4 Sino-Korean nominalizers -성/-적/-화 plus literal English -tion/-ment/-ness/-ity, cumulative 12+ per document → restore verb or adjective roots

tests.label: nominalization chain fails
tests.input: The implementation of the policy and the evaluation of the results took two quarters.

tests.label: plain verbs pass
tests.input: Policy took effect on Monday. We scored the results against last quarter.
